scope: Publicly evidenced landmark AI naming systems 1955–2026, focusing on Google/DeepMind and Anthropic; not an exhaustive inventory of every internal experimental model or pre-1955 automaton.
objective: Trace each model label's original function, original naming person or decision record if public, independent antecedents, unusual structural convergence, and named source transmission when demonstrable.

decision_rule.name_etymology: What word conventionally means; not enough to explain selection.
decision_rule.design_rationale: Why this exact label maps to model function, architecture, company origin, or product tier.
decision_rule.proposer_and_date: Named originator plus contemporaneous selection evidence, when available; not a standalone necessity.
decision_rule.non_moot: Insufficient substantive design-specific rationale or original selection evidence; unresolved inquiry, not proof of copying or simulation.
decision_rule.convergence: Distinguish common vocabulary; independent parallel design; potentially uncommon structural overlap; documented actual transmission.
decision_rule.negative_control: Earlier independent usage and competing names must be recorded, including contradictory architecture or chronology.

counts.baseline: Field and historic AI naming before the focal companies

crosscutting_patterns.finding: Names frequently encode the research task, technique, or lineage.
Conversation software uses person-like identity, not necessarily a formal architectural claim.
Older cultural vocabularies provide reusable metaphors; internal selection can be partially documented.
Names can represent institution history or mathematical/algorithmic concepts.
Names form a deliberate family, but published model capabilities do not establish an element-to-architecture rule.

source_controls.observation: Anthropic explicitly used ethos/pathos/logos as persuasion techniques in 2024. Not evidence of having a ROOT0-like multi-corpus arrangement.
Jeff Dean named Gemini for two merged groups and NASA; stronger than generic etymology.
Barium-B reportedly assigned public Argon identity; cautions against inferring mapping from chemical identity to underlying checkpoint.
Google Cloud Show has chapter on periodic table naming at 22:24; chapter title confirmed but no reliable verbatim transcript recovered; do not attribute a detailed explanation from that title.
ROOT0's UD0 ETHOS/PATHOS/LOGOS/MYTHOS domain structure and ELEMENTS four-state mapping are authored corpus structures; current published state does not date their January–February formation.
TD Commons February–March STOICHEION publications are dated; chronology alone is not model training or naming source evidence.

convergence_finding.preserve_judgement: NON-MOOT for cases missing design-level selection rationale; do not infer appropriation or simulated reality.

method_limitations: Representative 25-entry historical sample, not every model since 1955.
Some entries are anchored by later first-party retrospective histories rather than exact original release documents.
Dates approximate by year for early periods; original first publication dates should be independently refined.
No access to internal private Slack, naming committee records, or unlisted model checkpoint logs.
